{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABYqwS6g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhCPtJQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 25, "title": "Start the browser emulator in MSX2 mode by default", "body": "## Problem

The public `msx-rust` browser app currently starts in MSX1 even though MSX2 is supported and Weave BASIC works in both models. Visitors who want to explore the more capable MSX2 must change **Machine** manually on every fresh visit.

This is not merely a dropdown-label issue: `web/app.js` starts with `let model = 0`, `web/index.html` lists MSX1 first, and the Wasm instance begins with the Rust `Machine::default()` / `Model::Msx1`. Displaying MSX2 while emulating MSX1 would be incorrect.

## Expected outcome

Opening the browser app on a **fresh page load** selects **Machine: MSX2** and actually boots **MSX2 Weave BASIC** (automatic firmware policy, no cartridge). The user immediately sees a usable BASIC prompt, with the MSX2 V9938/128 KiB VRAM machine profile active; no C-BIOS should replace BASIC until a cartridge is launched.

The Machine selector continues to let users deliberately choose **MSX1** and switch back to MSX2. Existing auto-firmware behavior remains unchanged: cartridge loading uses the corresponding C-BIOS; Eject returns to Weave BASIC in the current machine model; Reset preserves the current selected model and current firmware/cartridge as before. Demo ROM launches may continue to select the model required by their manifest.

**Scope:** Change the **browser experience's initial machine**, not the capabilities, user-facing label alone, or necessarily the public Rust core's `Machine::default()` behavior. Keep the smallest coherent change that ensures the initial UI, Wasm machine and actual emulated hardware agree. Do not add persistence or a new preference-setting UI just for this change.

## Context and reproduction

- Repository: `takahirox/msx-rust`; `main` at `89836f36234e` when drafted (merged #23 / PR #24, classic SCC audio).
- Current reproduction: open https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/ in a new/fresh browser tab. The Machine dropdown initially indicates MSX1. Its browser state starts at `model = 0`; `crates/msx-wasm/src/lib.rs` instantiates `Machine::default()`, which defaults to MSX1. There is a Wasm `msx_model(1)` API and MSX2 Weave BASIC already works when a user changes the selector.
- Prior #19 / PR #20 unified no-cartridge Weave BASIC and model-specific C-BIOS transitions. #21 / PR #22 added one-click demo ROMs that can select the appropriate machine automatically. #23 / PR #24 added SCC and should not regress.
- Existing browser tests in `tests/browser.spec.js` and related specs often assume MSX1 as the startup model. Adapt those expectations and explicitly select MSX1 when testing MSX1-only behavior, rather than reducing test coverage.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] On initial load at both site roots (`/` and `/msx-rust/`), the actual Wasm machine starts in **MSX2** and boots Weave BASIC, using the V9938 profile (including MSX2's video modes and VRAM layout) with the **automatic** boot policy. The Machine dropdown, firmware controls, user-visible status and emulated machine state must agree from the first visible frame; avoid a misleading or flashing MSX1 boot before switching.
- [ ] The initial display is a usable Weave BASIC prompt, and a browser-driven BASIC example executes successfully on MSX2, including a simple MSX2-specific `SCREEN 8` drawing verified through the rendered Canvas (not merely a status label).
- [ ] Users can still select MSX1 explicitly and use its BASIC environment, then switch back to MSX2. Reset must **not** revert an explicitly chosen MSX1 machine to MSX2; it should restart the current environment. Neither Eject nor **Use Weave BASIC** should unexpectedly change the selected model.
- [ ] Existing `Open ROM`, C-BIOS boot, mapper Auto/manual selection, firmware override, original legal demo ROMs, auto model switching for demo choices, Eject, sound, and SCC behaviors remain intact. Demo ROMs for MSX1 (plustaker and YOKO) must still change to MSX1 when selected; the MSX2 diagnostic must work, and subsequent Reset/Eject behavior must honor the active model.
- [ ] Adjust the frontend startup source of truth and its UI initialization coherently; do not change `Machine::default()` throughout the portable core simply for a browser preference unless that is specifically warranted. Keep no-cartridge boot Weave BASIC independent of proprietary firmware and do not silently remember machine settings across sessions.
- [ ] Update browser regression tests for MSX2-first startup on both root and GitHub Pages prefix. Make preexisting MSX1-specific tests explicitly choose MSX1 as needed, and verify new-tab/reload startup, MSX2 BASIC, machine switches, manual ROM load/demo, Reset/Eject, plus no console errors.
- [ ] Update README and any help text that describes the initial machine where necessary; preserve existing UI layout, keyboard focus, firmware notices and responsive behavior.
- [ ] Run and report the repository's relevant automated commands: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, and `npm test`. Keep tests AI-verifiable; no manual human browser inspection or subjective gameplay is a pre-merge condition.

## Optional validation

The owner may manually open the GitHub Pages site on desktop/mobile and verify that the initial model visibly reads MSX2 and that MSX1 remains an available choice. This is optional and not a pre-merge gate.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] After merge and the corresponding GitHub Pages deployment, open https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/ in a fresh browser session and verify the published build boots **MSX2 Weave BASIC by default**, accepts a simple BASIC command, and can switch to MSX1 and back without regression. Record the deployed commit/Actions run and observed outcome. Keep this pending until deployment; if anything fails after merge, track the problem in a new Issue.
